steps.t: Discovery first: which device owns the routing decision — L3 switch, legacy firewall or Cato Socket?
An interconnect hub holds legacy CPE and a Socket; migrated sites reach legacy ones across its handoff.
Sites move in waves; rollback is a route change — re-add the dummy range or withdraw the BGP prefix.
Multi-region estates keep eBGP per regional hub so AS-PATH anchors each flow and its return symmetric.

steps.t: Manchester becomes the bridge: the first Socket goes in beside the MPLS CE and peers eBGP with it.
London DC and AWS eu-west-2 come on-net first; branches still on MPLS reach them across the handoff.
Bristol and Leeds swing up to the PoP in waves; Glasgow rides the emptying MPLS cloud until its turn.
The last circuit is switched off — every site, DC and cloud rides the Cato backbone, one routing table.
